div.head: II Cn 45
div.ab: Gyf man wealdan mæge, ne dýde man æfre on Sunnandæges freolse ænigne forwyrhtne man, butan he fleo oððe feohte; ac wylde ⁊ healde, þæt se freolsdæg agan sy.
Gif man wealdan mage, ne dyde man æfre on Sunnandages freolse ænigne forwyrhtne man, buton he fleo oððe feohte; ac wylde ⁊ healde, þæt se freolsdæg agan sy.
Et si uitari possit, numquam occidatur aliquis die Dominica morti deputatus (morte forisfactus), nisi fugiat uel repugnet; sed capiatur et seruetur, donec festum transierit.
Gyf man wealdan mæge, ne dyde man næfre on Sunnandæges freolse ǽnigne forworhtne man, buton he fleo oððe feohte, ac wylde man hine ⁊ healde þæt se freolsdæg agan sy.
Gyf man wealdan mæge, ne dyde man æfre on Sunnandæges freolse ænigne forwyrhtne man, butan he fleo oððe feohte; ac wylde and healde, þæt se freolsdæg agan sy.
If it can be so contrived, no condemned man shall ever be put to death during the Sunday festival, unless he flees or fights, but he shall be arrested and kept in custody until the festival is over.
If it can be managed, no one sentenced to death should ever be executed on a Sunday holy day, unless he flees or fights; but he is to be arrested and held until the holy day has ended.
If it can be arranged, no condemned man should ever be put to death during the Sunday festival, unless he flees or resists; but he is to be seized and kept until the feast-day is over.

Wenn es einzurichten möglich ist, richte man niemals in der Sonntagsfeier einen verurtheilten Menschen hin — ausser wenn er flieht oder ankämpft [gegen die Haft] —, sondern bewältige und halte [ihn fest, bis] dass der Feiertag vergangen ist.

If it can be managed, let no condemned man ever be put to death during the Sunday festival — unless he flees or fights [against arrest] —, but let him be overpowered and held [until] the feast-day has passed.
